newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco to reopen lists for eligible voters.
newsitem.headline: Morocco to reopen lists for eligible voters.

text.p: Morocco will reopen election lists on Thursday to allow voters to register for general elections scheduled for the second half of 1997, an official said on Wednesday.

An interior ministry spokesman said: "Election lists will be exceptionally opened from 10 to 14 April 1997 to enable Moroccan citizens, who missed the chance earlier, to register their names in conformity with the law's requirements."
Morocco's 333-seat parliament unanimously adopted last month a draft law on general elections in 25,000 communal and municipal centres, including the disputed Western Sahara.
With 125 seats, opposition groups led by the old-guard Istiqlal party voted in favour of the law, the ministry added.

Under the new law all Moroccans, from the age of 20, must vote in the elections, the ministry said. The law is part of constitutional reforms adopted in a 1996 referendum, which includes setting up a bicameral parliamentary system.

Parliament has also adopted a law on the regions aimed at reinforcing administrative decentralisation and transferring some state financial powers to local authorities, such as tax collection and means to build schools and hospitals, officials said.
